key_insight: A flow-based generative model can learn an approximate invariant probability distribution of turbulent channel flow, enabling realistic synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction from minimal observations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to generate physically consistent turbulent fields for simulation initialization, data augmentation, and reconstruction in fluid engineering workflows.
method: Train a flow-based generative model on a minimal conditional flow unit around a single center observation.
Define a consistent conditional sampling procedure to draw fields from the learned distribution.
Validate against direct numerical simulation for statistical, conditional, and dynamical fidelity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that generated fields reproduce key turbulence features, and when used as DNS initial conditions they produce physical, statistically stationary ensemble statistics.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated for turbulent channel flow at Re_tau = 180, so generalization to other Reynolds numbers, geometries, or higher-dimensional flow regimes still needs verification.
paper_title: A machine-learned probability distribution in the phase space of turbulent channel flow for synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction
